findings.title: The red/green command is the worker's choice and nothing ties it to the planned test
quotes: the red and green command comes from the worker, not from the task
accept red only when it exits non-zero and its output matches none of the known collection, import or syntax error patterns of that command's test runner
findings.fix: require the recorded command to run the TC-n named in the task's `Test:` line. Treat "no tests collected" and a non-test wrapper as refused for known runners. Say how the runner is detected when the command is wrapped.

sources.situation: nothing requires the command to run the task's TC-n or any test. A worker names `sh -c 'test -e src/new.py'`. Its runner is unknown, so FR-9 accepts red on exit code alone. Once the code exists, green exits 0, the guard passes, and the task is "proven" with no real test. A known runner has the same hole. `pytest -k nothing` exits 5 with "no tests ran", which is not in the error patterns, so FR-8 accepts it as red. Wrapping the runner in `bash run.sh` or `npm test` also turns it into an unknown runner and skips the import-error check. FR-34 only says "telling the runner from the command" and does not say how.

findings.reason: FR-8 only checks exit code and error patterns, and the Non-goals say the command "comes from the worker, not from the task". Nothing ties the command to the task's TC-n, so `pytest -k nothing` (exit 5, not an error pattern) or a non-test shell command passes red. The Risks section covers only the unknown-runner fallback, not this.
findings.note: Q17: red refuses no tests ran and a command not naming the planned test file (FR-8, FR-43, AC-43)

findings.title: Review passes when the suite breaks without a named failing test, or when tests are removed
quotes: the full test suite with no failure missing from the baseline
a failing test that the baseline doesn't list
findings.fix: for known runners too, treat a non-zero suite exit with no failure named in the baseline as a new failure. Also fail the review when the suite's test count drops below the baseline, or when a baseline-passing test is no longer collected.

sources.situation: a worker's change breaks an import in another test module. The suite exits non-zero at collection, with no individually named failing test. Or the worker deletes, skips or xfails an existing test. Under the review rule, "no failing test missing from the baseline" holds, so the review passes and the task is committed. FR-36 closes this only for unknown runners ("any non-zero suite exit"). For known runners, whether a collection error, crash, timeout or removed test counts as a "failure" is unspecified. SC-1's "passed review" then means little. A baseline-failing test that now fails for a different reason is also masked, because failures are compared by name.

findings.reason: FR-14, FR-17 and the Review decision table compare "failing tests" by name against the baseline. FR-36 handles only unknown runners ("any non-zero suite exit"). For known runners, a collection crash, a removed test or a different failure reason is not addressed anywhere.
findings.note: Q18: the review also fails on a collection or import error or fewer tests than the baseline (FR-14, AC-44)

findings.title: The guards rest on history.jsonl and state.json, which a worker can write or unblock, and only the card text forbids it
quotes: The card forbids the worker to edit `state.json` or `history.jsonl`, or to run any other `nio flow` command.
derive each task's status from history lines
WHEN the human runs `nio flow unblock <slug> T-n --human`
findings.fix: make the review fail on a worker-written change to `history.jsonl`, `state.json`, `contracts.md` or `tests.md`. Say how `--human` is made unforgeable by an agent, for example a check the CLI can make about who is calling. Or state that this is an accepted risk in "Risks and evidence against".

sources.situation: a worker has a shell and write access. It appends a green line to `history.jsonl`, or runs `nio flow unblock <slug> T-3 --human`. The unblock resets the attempt count to 0 and drops the frozen files, which undoes both the 3-attempt cap (FR-26) and the test freeze. The CLI cannot tell the worker from the human. Status then reads `done`, SC-1's trace is forged, and the only protection is a prompt line. AC-21 covers handoff text but not a forged history line. FR-25 flags changes to spec, plan or tasks, but not to `state.json` or `history.jsonl`. FR-25's "plan files" may also leave out `contracts.md` and `tests.md`, which are in the worker's own pack and which it could weaken.

findings.reason: FR-5 forbids editing `state.json` or `history.jsonl` only in the card text. FR-25 checks only spec, plan and tasks, and "plan files" does not clearly cover `contracts.md` or `tests.md`. FR-38 gives the CLI no way to tell the worker from the human. The accepted risk about hostile `--run` commands does not mention forged state. The point is weak but not refuted.
findings.note: Q19: the review also fails on changes to contracts.md and tests.md (FR-25, AC-45); forged progress files and unblocks accepted as a risk

findings.title: The commit lands wherever HEAD is, or does not land, while the task is already done
quotes: mark it done and make one commit with the message `T-n: <title>` on the effort branch
SHALL never commit a task on the default branch
findings.fix: check the current branch is `nio/<slug>` at every claim and at commit time, and refuse otherwise. Specify commit failure as a refused or retryable state in which the task is not `done`. Define the order of the history write and the commit.

sources.situation: (a) the branch is checked only "WHEN the implement stage starts ... on its default branch". Say the human checks out main between tasks, the repo starts on another feature branch, or HEAD is detached. The next task's commit then goes onto main or the wrong branch, and FR-20's "never" is broken. (b) The commit can fail: a pre-commit hook rejects it, git identity is missing, or the process dies after the history line is written. AC-26 says the commit holds the history line, so the done line and the commit cannot be atomic. The state table has no row for a failed commit, so the task reads `done` with no `T-n` commit and nobody is told.

findings.reason: FR-20 checks the branch only "WHEN the implement stage starts while the repo is on its default branch", yet says "never commit a task on the default branch". Later HEAD moves are not covered. FR-19 and AC-26 put the history line inside the commit, and the state table has no failed-commit row.
findings.note: Q20: branch checked at every claim and commit; a failed commit keeps the task green and waits (FR-19, FR-20, AC-46, AC-47)

findings.title: A filed spec problem has no human notice or wait, and filing again creates a second record
quotes: WHEN the orchestrator files a blocked handoff's change request as a `C-*` record THE SYSTEM SHALL set the task to blocked.
a task blocked by a spec problem uses no attempt
findings.fix: on filing, set the effort waiting for the human and name the task and the `C-*` record. Make a repeat filing of the same handoff create no second record. Say what stops a worker from using `blocked` to avoid the attempt cap, for example the human sees each filing, or a limit per task.

sources.situation: FR-24 sets the task to blocked but does not notify the human or set the effort waiting. Only FR-26 does that, and only for the attempt cap. Independent tasks keep running, dependents of the blocked task never become ready, and the epic never finishes. If nothing else is ready, `next` has no defined answer, so the effort stalls silently with a `pending` change request the human has not been told about. UJ-2 step 3 ends "the human decides the change" with no mechanism that gets it to the human. Two further problems:

findings.reason: FR-24 only sets the task to blocked. The notify or waiting behaviour is in FR-26 (attempt cap) and FR-28 (epic), not in FR-24. UJ-2 step 3 says "the human decides" with no mechanism. The "Two further problems:" in the situation is cut off, but the main gap stands.
findings.note: Q21: filing a spec problem sets the effort waiting; a repeat filing makes no second record (FR-24, AC-48)

findings.title: Worker card forbids the nio flow calls that single mode needs
quotes: never run `nio flow` and never edit `state.json` or `history.jsonl`
it runs `nio flow` only for `red` and `green` on its own task in single mode
findings.fix: rewrite AC-2's Observable to match FR-5: the card forbids editing `state.json` or `history.jsonl` and any `nio flow` command other than `red` and `green` on its own task in single mode.

sources.situation: the card AC-2 describes tells the worker never to run `nio flow`. A single-mode worker, under A-3, FR-42 and accepted C-261029-rmbs, must run `nio flow red` and `nio flow green` on its own task. A card built to AC-2 blocks the single-mode path the spec requires.

AC-2 tests that the card says "never run `nio flow`". A-3 and FR-42 need the single-mode worker to run `nio flow red` and `nio flow green`. FR-5 says "any other `nio flow` command", so it permits those two. Cards exist per tier, not per mode, so one card has to carry both rules. A card that passes AC-2 would stop single mode working (AC-42). A card that supports AC-42 fails AC-2.

findings.reason: AC-2's Observable says the card tells the worker to "never run `nio flow`", while A-3, FR-42 and AC-42 need the single-mode worker to run `nio flow red` and `nio flow green`. FR-5 says "any other `nio flow` command".
findings.note: AC-2's Observable now matches FR-5: no nio flow command other than red and green on its own task in single mode

findings.title: State table's claimed row ignores mode, against FR-41
quotes: in split and single mode it SHALL refuse green on a claimed task, saying no failing test came first
| claimed | ignore | reject: already claimed | → red | → green | ignore | ignore | → blocked | → blocked | ignore | [human] |
findings.fix: add a mode condition to the claimed row, or a note under the table that FR-41 overrides the red and green columns for each mode.

sources.situation: a split-mode task is claimed and a green report arrives with no red first. The table says green is accepted (`→ green`), while FR-41 says refuse. A direct-mode task is claimed and a red report arrives. The table says red is accepted (`→ red`), while FR-41 says refuse. The table has no mode column, so one implementation cannot satisfy both.

the table sends `claimed` to `green` on a green report and to `red` on a red report, with no mode condition. FR-41 refuses green on `claimed` in split and single mode, and red in direct mode. So the table is wrong for two of three modes in each case. There is a second problem in direct mode.

findings.reason: The `claimed` row of the Task state table has `→ red` and `→ green` with no mode column. FR-41 refuses green on `claimed` in split and single mode, and refuses red in direct mode. Nothing says FR-41 overrides the table.
findings.note: Q22: modes note under the state table; a direct-mode failed review goes back to claimed (FR-45, AC-50)

findings.title: Attempt cap: AC-23 gives a fourth attempt, the Attempt entity blocks on the third
quotes: Given a task that has used 3 attempts, when its next attempt fails, then it is blocked
the third blocks the task
WHEN a task has failed 3 attempts THE SYSTEM SHALL set it to blocked
findings.fix: pick one count. If the third failure blocks, reword AC-23 to "has used 2 attempts, when its next attempt fails".

sources.situation: attempts 1, 2 and 3 all fail. Under AC-23 the task has used 3 attempts, so a fourth attempt runs before it blocks. Under the Attempt entity the third failure blocks it. Under FR-26 it blocks once it has "failed 3 attempts", which is after the third failure. An implementer following AC-23 will allow a fourth attempt, and one following the entity will not.

FR-26 and the Attempt entity block the task at the third failed attempt. The state "3 attempts used, task still open" in AC-23's Given therefore cannot occur, because the task was blocked when the third attempt failed. AC-23 only works if the fourth failure blocks. With attempts 0, 1, 2 used and the third failing, FR-26 says the task is blocked now. Read literally, AC-23 says it is not blocked until a fourth.

A task fails three times. Key entities and FR-26 ("failed 3 attempts") block it at the third failure. AC-23 starts from 3 attempts already used and blocks on the next failure, which is the fourth. A test written from AC-23 passes an implementation that gives a fourth try. A test written from the entity definition fails that same implementation. AC-36 and AC-37 count attempts in `state.json`, so the off-by-one shows in their expected values as well.

findings.reason: AC-23 starts from "has used 3 attempts" and blocks on the next failure, which is the fourth. FR-26 and the Attempt entity ("the third blocks the task") block at the third failure. The "3 attempts used, still open" state cannot occur under FR-37 and FR-26.
findings.note: AC-23 now starts from 2 attempts used, the third failure blocks, matching FR-26 and the Attempt entity

findings.title: AC-16 sends the status to a `review` state the table doesn't have
quotes: status leaves `review` as the state table says
findings.fix: name the status AC-16 expects, for example "status stays `green`", and check it against the green row.

sources.situation: the Task state table has no `review` state. Its states are pending, ready, claimed, red, green, done and blocked, and review is a column of events on the green row. Read literally, AC-16 names a state the table does not define, so a tester cannot tell whether the expected status is `green`, `red` or `done`.

The Task state table has the states pending, ready, claimed, red, green, done and blocked. `review` is not one of them. A failed review goes green → red, and the table only gives that transition for a review failure. A test can't assert "leaves review". The AC also doesn't say which status the task ends in, and that status is the thing under test.

findings.reason: AC-16's Observable says "status leaves `review` as the state table says", but the Task state table has no `review` state. Its states are pending, ready, claimed, red, green, done and blocked, and the green row's `review fails` column gives `→ red`. A tester cannot tell the expected end status from the AC. J-21 was merged into this finding.
findings.note: AC-16's Observable now names the end status, red with the attempt count up by 1, from the state table's green row

findings.fix: name C-261029-4cev as a prerequisite of this stage, or add an AC that a claim on a task with no `Mode:` line is refused.

only tasks the re-approved `tasks.md` adds or changes run, as new tasks

With a new ID, "T-2's new version" and the "T-2" the ACs use are not the same task.

findings.title: One effort carries five separable deliverables and 42 FRs

Most flexible; costs a change request to the tasks spec." (answers.md, Q14, a change request is what the human accepted for the three modes)

sources.situation: the spec bundles the task machine and guards (FR-3, FR-8 to FR-13, FR-17, FR-18, FR-26, FR-32, FR-37, FR-38), worker packs and cards (FR-4 to FR-7, FR-40 to FR-42), the commit and branch (FR-19 to FR-22), the baseline and suite (FR-16, FR-17, FR-35, FR-36), and the epic and effort hand-off (FR-27 to FR-31).
